IR.rationale: Bull steepening with falling short rates marks monetary easing. Easing changes funding costs and risk appetite for leveraged arbitrage and directional strategies.

B.rationale: Broad widening of high-yield and EM credit yields signals tighter credit and liquidity. Through stale pricing and slow mark-to-market this feeds into later returns of credit-sensitive strategies (distressed, event driven, convertible arbitrage).

V.rationale: A high VIX embeds a large variance risk premium. Hedge funds that implicitly sell volatility or supply liquidity tend to earn higher subsequent returns when it is elevated.

AP.rationale: Hedge fund returns load on lagged equity returns because of illiquid holdings and smoothed reporting. Joint strength in US and EM equities marks global risk-on.

TF.rationale: High stock trend-following straddle payoffs indicate large equity moves and dislocations (Fung–Hsieh factor). These relate to both CTA performance and stress for other styles.

ST.rationale: Equity long/short and many quantitative funds carry momentum exposure. Persistent momentum profits support their returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening yen together with a strengthening AUD is a carry-friendly, risk-on currency state that supports macro and carry-exposed funds.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity strength reflects global growth and trending markets that benefit macro and CTA strategies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with weak activity mark funding-constrained, deteriorating environments. These matter for leveraged hedge fund returns.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge fund index returns are positively autocorrelated because of illiquidity and return smoothing (Getmansky, Lo and Makarov).

IR.rationale: A falling 1Y–Fed Funds spread means markets are pricing rate cuts, which typically happens as stress builds.

B.rationale: Rising high-yield yields signal deleveraging and liquidity withdrawal, which precede large drawdowns in arbitrage and credit strategies.

V.rationale: High equity volatility combined with crisis-driven news volatility identifies systemic stress regimes in which left-tail outcomes cluster.

AP.rationale: Weak recent equity returns raise downside risk through lagged exposure, margin calls and forced selling.

TF.rationale: High lookback-straddle payoffs on stocks indicate violent market moves that hurt short-volatility hedge fund styles.

ST.rationale: Poor momentum returns signal crowded-trade unwinds and momentum crashes that damage equity long/short and quant funds.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects carry-trade unwinding and flight to safety, a classic precursor of hedge fund losses.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices signal weakening global demand and pressure on EM- and commodity-exposed positions.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress tightens funding and prime-broker terms, raising the probability of large losses for levered strategies.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent performance persists because of smoothing, and it triggers redemptions and fire sales.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening accompanies policy easing and recovery phases in which hedge funds rebound strongly.

B.rationale: Credit yield spikes create cheap distressed and convertible assets whose subsequent rebound produces right-tail returns.

V.rationale: High volatility widens the whole return distribution, raising the chance of large gains as well as large losses, especially for CTAs and liquidity providers.

AP.rationale: Strong broad and small-cap equity rallies mark risk-on recoveries that lift long-biased and event-driven funds.

TF.rationale: Strong bond trends deliver large payoffs to trend followers and macro funds.

ST.rationale: Persistent momentum profits indicate trending equity markets that favour long/short and systematic strategies.

FX.rationale: Strong currency trends generate large gains for CTAs and global macro funds.

COM.rationale: Commodity booms create trending markets and reflationary conditions that produce outsized gains.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions set the stage for high expected returns and sharp rebounds once liquidity returns.

ENDG.rationale: Return persistence makes strong recent performance predictive of continued large gains.
